A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TREAD, with the same research identity and substantially overlapping methods and experiments. All pages, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison despite the extensive revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original diffusion-training experiments, benchmark FIDs, routing ablations, RWKV results and generated samples, including additional evaluations in the appendix.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results, routing analyses, flow-matching experiments, REPA combinations and guidance evaluations in the main text and appendix.

M1.justification: V1 develops consecutive routes, addition of input tokens to intermediate features, and a weighted multi-route denoising/MAE loss. V2 instead presents a single identity-bypass route with one reconstruction loss applied uniformly to all tokens (Section 3). It also introduces training variants combining TREAD with REPA and subsequent fine-tuning without routing.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate class-conditional ImageNet-256 and ImageNet-512 generation and MS-COCO text-to-image generation. Flow-matching models, REPA combinations and guidance changes retain this dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: REPA becomes an evaluated comparator in v2 Tables 1 and 3. Guided comparisons expand beyond v1's DiT comparison to include MDT, MaskDiT, SD-DiT and SiT. Conversely, ADM, ADM-U, LDM-4 and LDM-8 disappear from the comprehensive benchmark comparison. SiT's unguided XL baseline was already present in v1 Table 10.

E3.justification: V2 adds flow-matching configurations, DiT-L experiments, extended training budgets, interval guidance, and 75K steps of fine-tuning without routing using batch size 1,024 and learning rate 1e-5. Route-location evaluation changes from the S/4, FID@10K setup stated in v1 Table 6 to DiT-B/2 with FID@5K in v2 Figure 8. The additional quality metrics were already reported in v1's appendix.

E4.justification: V2 replaces the multi-route loss and feature-addition ablations with substantially expanded route-placement analyses, correlations involving early loss, comparisons of routed layer similarities, and absolute-versus-relative route extrapolation to larger models. Table 3 additionally tests compatibility with REPA. Selection-rate and guidance analyses remain but report revised evidence.

E5.justification: V2 Figure 6 newly reports numerical correlation estimates and fitted trends relating route length, early training loss and FID. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: At 400K iterations, v1's DiT-XL/2+TREAD-2 reports FID 10.63, while v2's revised TREAD reports 7.38; these represent different method configurations. V2 adds longer-training results of 3.93 unguided and fine-tuned results of 2.09 guided or 1.69 with interval guidance, alongside new SiT, REPA and routing results. RWKV's 53.79 and the ImageNet-512/MS-COCO FIDs are retained, while the latter experiments' FLOPS entries are removed.

T1.justification: V1's mask operators, feature-combination definition and multi-route ensemble construction are replaced by a layer-composition definition of identity bypass and a uniform objective in v2 Equations 3–5. The forward/reverse-SDE, probability-flow and score derivation is removed, while the appendix's EDM sampling equations remain. Neither version contains original theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim of faster, better training without architectural changes remains. However, v1's multi-route contribution and robustness to largely arbitrary route locations give way to empirically derived placement guidelines and compatibility with representation distillation. Headline speedups change from 9.55/25.39 times to 14/37 times, with new guided and unguided quality claims.

C2.justification: V2 replaces v1's emphasis on repeatedly supplying noise-space information with an explanation based on variable computational depth and alternative token pathways. It interprets route length as underlying the loss–FID association and gives more restrictive placement guidance. It also newly discusses degraded guidance response, fine-tuning benefits and mixed-precision instability near late route endpoints.

D1.justification: V2 adds the exact VAE checkpoint, an fp32 stabilization measure, and Table S8 documenting model dimensions, heads, depths, revised routes and fine-tuning settings. V1's forward-pass pseudocode and explicit RWKV route listing disappear. The abstract changes from promising a code release to presenting code access; availability is not independently verified.

R1.justification: V2 broadens its positioning around the efficiency–effectiveness trade-offs of masking, architectural changes and teacher distillation, explicitly presenting TREAD as complementary to REPA. It adds context and citations concerning fine-tuning, personalization, guidance and residual architectures. REPA and SiT were already cited in v1; their increased prominence is not a first citation.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, method narrative and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. The separate Prerequisites section is absorbed into a shorter method introduction, and the appendix is reorganized around implementation, hyperparameters and guidance. The author list and affiliation also change.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the routing schematic, changes Figure 1 to a logarithmic compute axis, expands the similarity visualization, and introduces correlation and route-placement plots. Benchmark tables are reorganized into guided/unguided and architecture comparisons. V1's selected appendix sample grids are replaced by six uncurated sample collages, with another selected grid added to the main text.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evidence and practical guidance behind TREAD: systematic placement and scale-transfer analyses replace v1's largely arbitrary route-choice advice, while flow-matching and REPA experiments test broader applicability. The simpler objective and added stability and fine-tuning details improve understanding and usability. Removing pseudocode and some older comparators loses useful detail, but these losses do not outweigh the stronger methodological support.
